WYBOT and Aiper both make cordless robots that clean the pool floor, walls and waterline, plus solar skimmers for the surface; Betta makes solar surface skimmers only. Choose by the job: a WYBOT or Aiper robot for the floor and walls, and a Betta, WYBOT F1 or Aiper EcoSurfer for leaves and pollen on the surface.

What does each brand actually make?

It helps to separate two kinds of machine before comparing brands. A robotic pool cleaner runs underwater: it scrubs and vacuums the floor, and most models also climb the walls and clean the waterline, where the scum line forms. A robotic skimmer floats on the surface and catches leaves, bugs and pollen before they sink. Neither replaces the other, and many owners run one of each.

WYBOT Aiper Betta
Underwater robots A1, B1, C1, C2, C2 Vision, S2, S2 Solar, S2 Solar Vision, S3 Scuba 800, N1 Plus, N3, X1 Pro Max None
Surface skimmers F1 (solar) EcoSurfer M2 (solar) SE, SE Plus, Flex, Neo (solar)
Largest rated pool 3,230 sq ft (S2 models) 3,230 sq ft (Scuba X1 Pro Max) Not rated by area
Warranty 1 year (A1, B1, F1) or 2 years (other robots) Aiper manufacturer warranty 1 year
Shipping from us Free, continental US Free on most Aiper products Free ground, contiguous US

All figures come from WYBOT, Aiper and Betta. Pool sizes are the makers' ratings for each model.

Which floor robot fits my pool size?

Makers rate their robots by pool area in square feet. Measure your pool's length and width and multiply; for a freeform pool, a rough rectangle around the widest points is close enough to choose a size. Then pick a model rated above your pool, not right at the limit.

Pool size WYBOT Aiper
Flat above-ground, up to about 860 to 1,076 sq ft A1 (floor, up to 1,076 sq ft) Scuba 800 (flat floors, up to 860 sq ft)
Up to about 1,150 sq ft, whole pool B1
In-ground, up to about 1,600 sq ft C1 (up to 1,615 sq ft) Scuba N1 Plus (up to 1,600 sq ft)
Up to about 2,150 sq ft C2 or C2 Vision (up to 2,152 sq ft)
Large, up to about 3,230 sq ft S2, S2 Solar, S2 Solar Vision Scuba X1 Pro Max

The Aiper Scuba N3 is rated to plan its own cleaning route with Aiper's AI vision, and the WYBOT S3 maps the pool and empties its debris into a bin on its dock; both are for owners who want the least hands-on routine.

Floor only, or walls and waterline too?

The entry models clean the floor. The WYBOT A1 is built for the floor of flat-bottom pools, and the Aiper Scuba 800 for flat floors up to 860 sq ft. Every other WYBOT robot in our range, from the B1 up, also climbs the walls and cleans the waterline, and so does the Aiper Scuba N1 Plus. The Aiper Scuba X1 Pro Max adds the surface as well, per Aiper, so one robot covers floor, walls, waterline and surface.

  • Floor of a flat pool: WYBOT A1 or Aiper Scuba 800
  • Floor, walls and waterline: WYBOT B1 and up, or Aiper Scuba N1 Plus
  • Floor, walls, waterline and surface in one robot: Aiper Scuba X1 Pro Max

How do I measure my pool?

For a rectangular pool, multiply length by width: a 16 by 32 foot pool is 512 sq ft, and a 20 by 40 foot pool is 800 sq ft. For an oval, multiply length by width and then by about 0.8. For a round above-ground pool, multiply the diameter by itself and then by about 0.785; a 24 foot round pool is roughly 450 sq ft. For a freeform or kidney shape, take the longest length and the widest width and treat it as a rectangle; that slightly overstates the area, which is the safe direction when choosing a robot.

Also note the depth, the shape of the floor and anything a robot will meet: steps, a sun shelf, a deep end slope, or an attached spa. The makers' ratings assume a typical pool, so a pool with a large shallow shelf or many steps is worth mentioning when you ask for advice.

What about above-ground pools?

Above-ground pools usually have a flat floor and softer walls, and the entry robots are built for exactly that. The WYBOT A1 is designed for the floor of flat-bottom pools up to 1,076 sq ft, and the Aiper Scuba 800 for flat floors up to 860 sq ft, per their makers. If your above-ground pool is larger, or you want the walls and waterline cleaned too, check each model's product page for the pool types its maker lists before you choose. On the surface, the Betta SE Plus is worth a look for shallow areas, since Betta rates it for water as shallow as 3.5 inches.

How do they charge?

Most cordless robots come out of the pool to charge between cycles. Two WYBOT designs change that routine. The S2 Solar models return to a solar-powered charging dock, and the S3 docks and empties its debris into a bin on the deck. Camera models, the WYBOT C2 Vision and S2 Solar Vision, add a camera that targets dirty areas.

The skimmers all run on sunlight. Aiper says the EcoSurfer M2 skims for more than 35 hours per battery and tops up in the sun. Betta says a full charge runs its skimmers for 30 hours or more, so they keep going through the night, and the SE Plus and Neo add a wall adapter for cloudy stretches.

Which skimmer: Betta, WYBOT F1 or Aiper EcoSurfer?

If leaves, pollen and bugs are your main problem, the surface is where to start, because debris caught on top never reaches the floor. Betta is the specialist here, with four models that share the same solar skimming and differ in charging, control and the pools they suit:

Betta model Charging Control Good to know
SE Solar Wireless remote Simple solar skimming
SE Plus Solar plus wall adapter Wireless remote Works in water as shallow as 3.5 in
Flex Solar Runs by itself The Betta rated for infinity edge pools
Neo Solar plus wall adapter Betta app, 600 ft Gateway App control and scheduling

Betta rates its skimmers for saltwater pools up to 5,000 ppm salt. The WYBOT F1 and Aiper EcoSurfer M2 do the same surface job and are natural partners for a robot from the same brand; WYBOT sells Full Pool Solution bundles that pair a floor robot with the F1 in one order.

Do I need a robot and a skimmer?

Not always. If your pool sits in the open with few trees, a floor robot on a regular cycle may be all you need. If trees overhang the pool, or pollen coats the water in spring, a skimmer catches most of it before it sinks, and the floor robot then has less to do. Pools with both problems are the ones where owners pair the two, either with a WYBOT Full Pool Solution bundle or by choosing a robot and a skimmer separately.

  • Open pool, little debris: a floor robot
  • Trees and pollen, clean floor: a skimmer
  • Both: a robot plus a skimmer, or the Aiper Scuba X1 Pro Max, which Aiper rates for the surface too

What about shipping, warranty and parts?

Shipping and warranty differ by brand, so they are worth comparing alongside the specs. WYBOT ships free within the continental US and quotes 3 to 7 business days after processing; it does not ship to Alaska, Hawaii, Rhode Island, US territories or PO boxes. Aiper ships free on most products, usually in 10 to 14 business days. Betta ships free by ground within the contiguous US and usually dispatches in 1 to 2 business days.

WYBOT gives 1 year on the A1, B1 and F1 and 2 years on its other robots; Betta gives 1 year on every model; Aiper robots carry Aiper's manufacturer warranty. For Aiper, we also carry replacement parts such as chargers, debris baskets and filters, each named for the Scuba models it fits.

How much looking after do they need?

Every robot and skimmer collects debris in a basket or filter that needs emptying, and how often depends on your trees and the season. Most floor robots come out of the water to have their basket emptied; the WYBOT S3 is the exception, emptying its own debris into a bin on its dock. Skimmers hold what they catch in a basket on the surface unit, which is quick to lift out and rinse.

  • Empty the basket or filter after each cleaning cycle, or when the maker's app or indicator says so
  • Rinse fine filters so they keep catching dust and pollen
  • Keep solar panels clean so skimmers and solar docks charge fully
  • Follow each maker's winter storage advice when the pool closes

None of these machines replace your pool's filter, pump or water chemistry. They take the physical debris out, so the rest of the system has less to deal with.

So which should you choose?

For a lawn over an acre, the right robot mower comes down to three things: how much ground it covers per day, how steep your slopes are, and whether you want it to drive itself or ride along on a remote. Yarbo's RTK-mapped mowers run without a boundary wire, while Mowrator's remote control mowers climb steeper grades and push through rougher, taller growth.

How much lawn do you actually have to mow?

Before you compare a single spec, walk the property with a tape measure or pull up a satellite map and trace the mowed area. Subtract the driveway, beds, patio and any wooded sections you do not cut. If the lawn splits into separate zones connected by a path or gate, note that too, since it affects how a mower gets from one section to the next.

  • Walk the perimeter and mark where turf ends and beds, gravel or woods begin.
  • Measure or estimate square footage, then convert to acres.
  • List any separate zones, side yards or back lots that are not connected in one open stretch.
  • Note the steepest section by eye, even roughly, since slope changes which machine can do the job.

Once you know your real mowed acreage, you can match it against what each machine is rated to cover.

Autonomous vs remote control: what's the real difference on a big property?

The Yarbo Y40 Lawn Mower Pro and the Yarbo Y40P Lawn Mower Pro are autonomous. Yarbo maps your property with RTK and stereo vision instead of a buried boundary wire, and the mower runs its own schedule and finds its way back to charge. That means less hands-on time overall, but it also means the mower is doing the driving on its own across your whole lawn, including any tricky corners.

The Mowrator S1 21" 4WD and the Mowrator S1 21" 4WD Wide Wheels Edition are remote control mowers. There is no RTK, no app and no fuel to manage. You steer with a controller that Mowrator rates for a 5 ms response time and an interference-resistant signal, which matters if you are working close to the machine on a slope or around obstacles you want to avoid by eye.

  • Choose autonomous if you want the mower to run its schedule without you present.
  • Choose remote control if you want direct, real-time control over where the blade goes, especially on rough or overgrown ground.
  • Either type can suit a large property, the choice comes down to how hands-on you want to be.

How steep are your slopes?

Slope rating is one of the first numbers to check on a large or hilly property. Per Yarbo, both the Y40 and Y40P Core units climb up to 70% grade, or 35 degrees. Per Mowrator, the S1 21" 4WD is rated for a 75% grade, or 37 degrees, and the S1 21" 4WD Wide Wheels Edition raises that to an 85% grade, or 40 degrees, thanks to a wider tread that spreads the machine's weight for grip on soft, wet or uneven ground.

If slope is your main concern, read this guide on mowing steep slopes safely before you decide, since a slope rating on paper does not account for wet grass, loose soil or a slope that changes pitch partway up.

What about rough ground, roots and obstacles?

Large properties are rarely flat and clean. Per Mowrator, the S1 21" 4WD clears obstacles up to 3.94 inches, which covers roots, ruts and curb edges that stop a push mower, and it can cut grass up to 51 inches tall with its 21-inch deck and 1,985 W peak cutting power. That combination matters if part of your property has gone unmown for a while or has scattered obstacles across the mowing path.

Yarbo's mowers rely on binocular cameras, ultrasonic sensors and a bumper for obstacle avoidance, and the Y40P adds a rated vertical obstacle clearance of 2 inches. Both Yarbo units carry an IPX6 rating, and the Y40P adds rain detection so it can respond to changing weather while it works.

Battery life and charge times for big lots

On a large lawn, how a mower charges matters as much as how it cuts. Per Yarbo, the Y40's Lawn Mower Pro Module runs up to 120 minutes per charge, covering about 0.25 acre, and recharges from 20 to 80% in 90 minutes with automatic, wireless docking. The Y40P covers slightly more per charge, about 0.3 acre, with the same 120-minute run time and 90-minute charge window, backed by a 1.38 kWh battery.

Both Mowrator batteries are swappable and rated for 1,500 or more cycles.

  • If your lawn takes more than one battery cycle to finish, check whether the mower auto-recharges and resumes, or whether you need to swap a battery by hand.
  • Cold or hot weather can affect run time, so check any stated operating temperature range for your climate.

Do you need an app and mapping, or just a remote?

Yarbo mowers connect through the app for scheduling and mapping, and the Y40P adds 4G, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi HaLow connectivity for more flexible setup. There is no boundary wire to bury, since positioning comes from RTK, stereo vision and an IMU.

Mowrator mowers skip the app entirely. Per Mowrator, setup involves no RTK, no app and no fuel, just a swappable battery and a handheld controller. That can suit a property where you would rather steer directly than wait on a mower to map itself, especially in a first season on rough or newly cleared ground.

Leaves, snow and other seasonal jobs

A large property usually means more than mowing. Per Mowrator, the S1 21" 4WD switches between mow, mulch, discharge, bag and leaf vacuum modes, and with the mulching blade it moves leaves at 931 CFM into a 70 liter collection bag. The same 4WD platform accepts Mowrator's Snow Plow Kit and Trailer Hitch Kit, so one machine can take on more than cutting grass.

Per Mowrator, the S1 21" 4WD's main machine, remote control and battery are covered for 2 years or 2,000 hours of use, whichever comes first, with the charger covered for 1 year. Blades, tires and other consumable parts can be exchanged within 30 days if they are not damaged by misuse, and proof of purchase is required. Commercial, agricultural or other income-generating use falls under a separate Mowrator contract. Mowrator mowers ship free on most orders and typically arrive in 7 to 10 business days.

  • Keep your order confirmation as proof of purchase for either brand.
  • Call +1 423-927-3776 with any delivery timing questions before or after your order ships.

If your priority is a mower that runs its own schedule across several acres without a wire, the Yarbo Y40 Lawn Mower Pro or the higher-coverage Yarbo Y40P Lawn Mower Pro are built for that. If your ground is steep, rough, or overgrown and you want to steer around obstacles yourself, the Mowrator S1 21" 4WD or the higher-slope Mowrator S1 21" 4WD Wide Wheels Edition are worth a closer look. A pool skimmer removes leaves, bugs and pollen from the water surface before they sink. Most pools have a built-in skimmer: an opening in the wall at the waterline with a basket that the pump pulls water through. A robotic solar skimmer is a floating robot that travels the surface and collects debris in its own basket, powered by the sun.

What does a pool skimmer do?

Its job is the surface. Leaves, insects, pollen and blossoms float for a while before they soak through and drop to the floor. A skimmer catches them in that window. Debris that reaches the floor is harder to remove and can stain, so surface skimming is one of the simplest ways to keep a pool clean.

How does the built-in skimmer in the pool wall work?

The built-in skimmer is part of the pool’s plumbing. It is a box set into the wall at the waterline, with a flap at the opening and a basket inside. When the pump runs, water is pulled through the opening, the basket traps the debris, and the water continues to the filter.

  • It only works while the pump runs. Debris that lands when the pump is off keeps floating.
  • It only pulls from nearby water. Debris in corners or far from the opening can drift for a long time.
  • The basket needs emptying. A full basket slows the flow.

What is a robotic pool skimmer?

A robotic skimmer is a small floating robot. It moves around the surface on its own, scoops debris into an onboard basket, and runs on solar power, with no hose or cable. Because it travels, it reaches corners and the far side of the pool, and it keeps working when the pump is off.

Robotic skimmer or floor robot: which one do I need?

They do different jobs. A skimmer works on the surface. A floor robot cleans the floor, walls and waterline, which is where debris ends up once it sinks. Many pools with trees nearby use both: the skimmer catches most of the leaves first, and the floor robot handles what gets past it. Our guide WYBOT vs Aiper vs Betta compares both types by pool size.

How do the robotic skimmers we carry compare?

All details are from Betta, WYBOT and Aiper. We only list what each maker publishes.

What are the Betta skimmers like?

Betta makes four solar skimmers. The SE is solar powered with twin salt chlorine tolerant motors, automatic surface cleaning, a fine mesh debris basket and a wireless remote. The SE Plus adds a wall adapter, so it can charge from the outlet on cloudy days. The Flex has a soft touch casing and Eco and Normal modes, and Betta rates it for infinity edge, in-ground and above-ground pools. The Neo is controlled from the Betta app through a Gateway. What does the WYBOT F1 add?

The WYBOT F1 runs on a 33 W solar panel and collects debris in a 7 L basket with a fine filter. WYBOT lists Smart and Standard cleaning modes, edge cleaning with obstacle avoidance, remote control from the WYBOT app, and a design that keeps debris in the basket with no backflow. It ships free in the continental US with a 1-year WYBOT warranty.

WYBOT also sells the F1 in bundles with its floor robots, such as the S2 Solar and F1 bundle, if you want surface and floor covered in one order.

What about the Aiper EcoSurfer M2?

Aiper rates the EcoSurfer M2 for 35+ hours per battery. When the battery runs low, its SolarSeeker feature looks for sun and it goes back to skimming after 15 minutes of solar charging. It also holds 3 in chlorine tablets in an adjustable dispenser, uses two optical sensors to avoid obstacles, and weighs 12.6 lb. Aiper covers it with a 2-year warranty.

Why does surface debris matter so much in fall?

In fall a single windy afternoon can drop more leaves on a pool than the built-in skimmer can take in before they sink. Wet leaves on the floor break down over time, can leave marks on light surfaces and give the filter more work. Catching them while they float is simpler than lifting them off the floor later. That is why a skimmer earns its keep in leaf season, even on pools that stay covered for part of the winter.

How do I look after the built-in skimmer?

  • Empty the basket often, more often in fall and after storms.
  • Check that the flap at the opening moves freely, so floating debris can get in.
  • Keep the water level around the middle of the skimmer opening. Too low and it pulls air, too high and it skims less.
  • Rinse the basket rather than knocking it against hard edges, which can crack it.

Where does a solar skimmer work best?

A solar skimmer needs light on its panel, so it does best on pools that get sun for a good part of the day. If trees or buildings shade the pool, choose a model with another way to charge, such as the Betta SE Plus with its wall adapter, or the Aiper EcoSurfer M2, which runs on its battery and looks for sun when it needs to top up. Leave it on the water during the day and let it roam; most of the work happens while debris is still landing.

Will a robotic skimmer work in a salt pool?

Betta lists twin salt chlorine tolerant motors on its SE, SE Plus and Flex, which are built for salt and chlorine pools. WYBOT says the F1 is built to endure sun, rain and chlorine. If you run a salt system, check the maker’s water ratings on the product page before you buy, and rinse the skimmer with fresh water when you take it out for the season.

Is a robotic skimmer hard to set up?

No wiring or plumbing is involved. Charge it, place it on the water, and it starts working. The app controlled models, the Betta Neo and the WYBOT F1, also let you start, stop or steer from your phone, and the Betta SE and SE Plus come with a remote. Empty the onboard basket the same way you would the one in the wall.

What does a skimmer not do?

A skimmer only sees the top of the water. It will not lift sand, dirt or leaves that have already settled on the floor, it will not scrub the walls, and it does not replace your pump and filter. Heavier debris, like acorns or small stones, sinks too fast for any skimmer to catch. It also does not balance your water, although the Aiper EcoSurfer M2 can carry chlorine tablets in its dispenser while it skims, per Aiper. Think of the skimmer as the first line: it cuts down how much reaches the floor, so the rest of your pool care has less to do.

How do a skimmer and a floor robot split the week?

The skimmer works every sunny day, catching debris as it lands. The floor robot runs on a schedule to clean what got past it and to brush the walls and waterline. Several floor robots let you set that schedule in an app: WYBOT lists up to 4 cleanings a week for the C2, and Aiper’s Eco mode on the Scuba N1 Plus cleans for 45 minutes every 48 hours, three times. With a skimmer on the surface, those floor runs have less to pick up. If you want both from one brand, WYBOT pairs the F1 with its floor robots in its Full Pool Solution bundles, and our pool robot comparison covers which floor robot suits which pool size.

Do I still need the built-in skimmer if I buy a robot?

Yes. The built-in skimmer is part of how water reaches your filter, so it stays. A robotic skimmer works alongside it: it covers the times the pump is off and the parts of the surface the built-in skimmer does not reach.

How do I choose a robotic skimmer?

  • Pool type: for an infinity edge pool, Betta lists the Flex.
  • Sun: if your pool is shaded, look at the SE Plus with wall charging, or the Aiper M2 with its battery.
  • Control: the Betta Neo and WYBOT F1 are app controlled, the Betta SE and SE Plus come with a remote.
  • Chlorine: the Aiper M2 doses chlorine tablets as it skims.
  • Floor too: pair a skimmer with a floor robot, or pick a WYBOT bundle.

Is a robotic skimmer hard to set up?

No wiring or plumbing is involved. Charge it, place it on the water, and it starts working. The app controlled models, the Betta Neo and the WYBOT F1, also let you start, stop or steer from your phone, and the Betta SE and SE Plus come with a remote. Empty the onboard basket the same way you would the one in the wall.

What does a skimmer not do?

A skimmer only sees the top of the water. It will not lift sand, dirt or leaves that have already settled on the floor, it will not scrub the walls, and it does not replace your pump and filter. Heavier debris, like acorns or small stones, sinks too fast for any skimmer to catch. It also does not balance your water, although the Aiper EcoSurfer M2 can carry chlorine tablets in its dispenser while it skims, per Aiper. Think of the skimmer as the first line: it cuts down how much reaches the floor, so the rest of your pool care has less to do.

How do a skimmer and a floor robot split the week?

The skimmer works every sunny day, catching debris as it lands. The floor robot runs on a schedule to clean what got past it and to brush the walls and waterline. Several floor robots let you set that schedule in an app: WYBOT lists up to 4 cleanings a week for the C2, and Aiper’s Eco mode on the Scuba N1 Plus cleans for 45 minutes every 48 hours, three times. With a skimmer on the surface, those floor runs have less to pick up. If you want both from one brand, WYBOT pairs the F1 with its floor robots in its Full Pool Solution bundles, and our pool robot comparison covers which floor robot suits which pool size.

Do I still need the built-in skimmer if I buy a robot?

Yes. The built-in skimmer is part of how water reaches your filter, so it stays. A robotic skimmer works alongside it: it covers the times the pump is off and the parts of the surface the built-in skimmer does not reach.

How do I choose a robotic skimmer?

  • Pool type: for an infinity edge pool, Betta lists the Flex.
  • Sun: if your pool is shaded, look at the SE Plus with wall charging, or the Aiper M2 with its battery.
  • Control: the Betta Neo and WYBOT F1 are app controlled, the Betta SE and SE Plus come with a remote.
  • Chlorine: the Aiper M2 doses chlorine tablets as it skims.
  • Floor too: pair a skimmer with a floor robot, or pick a WYBOT bundle.
